newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle end higher after $70 cash trades.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle end higher after $70 cash trades.

text.p: CME live cattle futures closed sharply higher, with December setting a contract high late, in reaction to active trading at $70.00 per cwt in cash feedlot markets, traders said.
Meat packing companies were aggressive buyers of October and December contracts late. Some traders said the buying was short covering, while others said it was new longs.
Futures sped higher near midsession in reaction to reports of active cattle sales at $70.00. Near the close, traders said feedlots will likely be pricing cattle at $71.00 next week.
Also, some cattle feeders said many of these cattle will be shipped Monday, much faster than the normal seven-day delivery schedule.
Feeder cattle futures closed higher, reflecting gains in live cattle, and in reaction to higher cash feeder prices, traders said.
The latest CME Feeder Cattle Index was 0.14 cent higher at 63.29 cents per lb.

Complementing the higher cash cattle prices was talk of higher beef prices next week in anticipation of supermarkets increasing beef featuring. Traders said beef should be widely advertised before October, which is National Pork Month.
Live cattle closed up 0.875 to 0.250 cent with October up 0.825 at 72.175 cents per lb and December up 0.875 at 68.575. December cattle set a contract high of 68.600 cents.
Feeder cattle closed up 0.825 to 0.200 cent with October up 0.825 at 64.275 cents a lb.
